q: A report with no detections ran for three minutes with no network. Which conclusion is defensible?
options: The object is safe for all devices and recipient workflows
The lack of network shows the artifact contains no active content
The test proves the employee saw the same behaviour on their laptop
No relevant behaviour observed under those conditions
explanation: The setup and observation window limit what a quiet run establishes.

q: Which sandbox report section shows parent and child processes?
options: The appendix listing all permitted network destinations
The static file digest roster presented before execution
The process tree with image and parent fields
The scoring section that summarises classifier names
explanation: The process tree supplies execution relationships the verdict alone cannot show.

q: An internal hash match exists but the report concerns a different file build. What should be checked next?
options: Whether the file's name resembles one in the approved report
Whether the exact bytes and report provenance match
Whether both reports used the same severity scale
Whether the employee received both files through the same gateway
explanation: A reproducible match needs the correct artifact and a traceable report.

q: What is the role of the controller before a new run?
options: Queue the request and prepare a clean guest
Assign the case severity after analysing the business impact
Verify which employee read the original message
Replace the report evidence with a final classification
explanation: The controller coordinates the execution environment and scheduling.

q: A report says a sandbox made a DNS query but recorded no response. What is the appropriate claim?
options: The operator returned a payload that the monitor could not identify
The sandbox confirmed subsequent credential entry at the destination
The network report proves the artifact had no ability to use DNS
A request was observed; remote behaviour remains unverified
explanation: An attempted lookup does not establish what a remote system returned.

q: Why preserve the report's run identifier and settings?
options: They verify that the same employee received all similar messages
They make it unnecessary to preserve any original file evidence
They make the scope of observations reviewable
They substitute for recording how the file was collected
explanation: A later analyst can identify the observed run and its limitations.

q: A potential invoice contains customer details. Which handling decision fits?
options: Submit to any service that promises reports quickly
Use an approved restricted workflow or escalate
Remove the file's name and send the unchanged contents publicly
Treat retention terms as irrelevant if a verdict is urgently needed
explanation: Data inside the file can remain sensitive after superficial changes.

q: A verdict is high severity but has sparse observable evidence. What should the case note preserve?
options: The classifier result, underlying observations and uncertainty
The classifier score as a conclusive statement of compromise
Only screenshots of the coloured result without the report ID
The report's final classification and no discussion of missing coverage
explanation: The verdict is an assessment whose supporting evidence matters.

q: Which regulator-independent control applies to partner-shared evidence?
options: Replace the sharing mark once an internal case is opened
Treat a public service as private when a submission page requires login
Assume the same access applies to an artifact and its public report
Observe the source's sharing restrictions and contract terms
explanation: Access and distribution restrictions follow the source and approved terms.

q: A report shows an Office process and a child script interpreter. How should the analyst use it?
options: Copy it as proof that the suspected user's workstation executed the same chain
Assume a generic word processor label identifies the malicious document exactly
Check the relationship and corroborate with the affected device's logs
Treat it as evidence that every recipient opened their copy of the message
explanation: Sandbox observations concern the run and can guide endpoint corroboration.

q: What does a file activity section describe?
options: The status of each message in the receiving user's mail client
Observed file creation, modification or deletion
Each unrelated file currently present on the employee's device
Whether the organisation can publish the file to a third-party service
explanation: It describes monitored effects inside the observed environment.

q: When is an external digest lookup itself sensitive?
options: When it could reveal interest in a distinctive restricted artifact
Only when digest length includes the complete original object
When two internal records already use different filenames
Never, because the lookup contains no direct file bytes
explanation: A lookup can disclose a unique association even without file content.

q: Why restore an analysis guest between submissions?
options: To cancel any business containment request raised from the earlier case
To regenerate the original messages delivered to employee accounts
To establish which third party controls each destination in the report
To reduce contamination across separate runs
explanation: A clean starting state helps attribute observations to the intended run.

q: A sandbox had no visibility into a particular system mechanism. What belongs in the result?
options: A clean verdict for every activity that did not appear in the report
An assertion that the questionable activity must have occurred
A stated collection gap and a separate corroboration plan
A deletion of the monitoring details from the analyst's notes
explanation: Lack of monitoring limits the conclusions that absence can support.

q: A service allows private reports but unclear sample retention. What should the analyst do?
options: Treat the login requirement as approval for all evidence classes
Check approval and retention terms before submission
Upload first and request privacy guidance only if the result is positive
Replace the original evidence ID to avoid associating the case with the upload
explanation: Authorization depends on the sample data and the service's actual terms.

q: Which evidence relates directly to network activity in one run?
options: Captured queries and connections from the observed guest
A filename selected by the person who submitted the sample
The visibility label on the metadata attached to the case record
The peer-review decision on whether containment should continue
explanation: Traffic capture records activity at the particular monitoring boundary.

q: An analyst has a short quiet run and suspicious endpoint telemetry. How should they proceed?
options: Close the case because dynamic analysis supersedes endpoint evidence
Reclassify the endpoint finding as a harmless training notification
Accept the document context only if another sandbox also finds no behaviour
Treat the run as inconclusive and investigate endpoint evidence
explanation: Independent device evidence may be more relevant to actual exposure.

q: What should an analyst prioritise when reading a verdict?
options: Rank it by the colour used in the summary widget
Compare the number of pages in competing vendor reports
Link it to the underlying observed events
Copy only the highest score into the executive case line
explanation: Underlying events let the analyst judge what supports the assessment.

q: A restricted artifact already has a reviewed internal report. What is the least-exposing first step?
options: Submit a new public copy to obtain an independent score immediately
Use the report after checking its artifact and context
Send the sample to each analyst for a separate workstation review
Forward the report externally before checking its sharing permission
explanation: Prior evidence can answer the analytical question without new disclosure.

q: A test had controlled simulated responses. What limitation should be documented?
options: It does not establish what a real service would return
It proves the live destination would always behave the same way
It cannot record a request unless the actual destination is visited
It confirms the attachment executed on the recipient's endpoint
explanation: Simulated response conditions belong to the test and constrain inference.

q: Which result would be recorded as registry evidence?
options: A report title copied from an earlier case or vendor portal
A clicked-link statement given by a payments approver
A query string preserved during static URL examination
A value change observed in the guest by the monitor
explanation: The registry section records observed key and value changes.

q: Two runs disagree and used different guest images. What is the best comparison?
options: Average the scores and use the mean as the only finding
Ignore configuration and trust the verdict recorded most recently
Compare input identity, environment and observations for each run
Compare the attachment names and retain only the more severe result
explanation: Differences in both environment and evidence can explain divergent results.

q: What should the case record contain after approved submission?
options: Only the resulting classifier label copied into the case subject
The service, artifact, reason, timestamp and submitting role
Only the approval thread without the related evidence identifier
A link to the service login page without any run identifier
explanation: Submission records support custody, reproducibility and data review.

q: A document exhibits no activity in the guest and the gateway trace is suspicious. What next?
options: Preserve the quiet result and review the independent evidence
Release the document because the guest recorded no process launch
Treat the trace and sandbox results as proof of the same file behaviour
Wait for a user to open the document again on their regular device
explanation: A sandbox result is one input and observed delivery context remains relevant.

q: Which audience should receive the full restricted report?
options: Every employee who might have seen a similar subject line
Any external recipient requesting proof of the final case result
The original distribution list of the suspicious message
The authorised investigators who need its details
explanation: Report details can expose the artifact, environment or individuals involved.
